unmatched_gold.description: asyncio.wait() is non-deterministic about which task runs first; forcing signal_to_start_request to await sleep is being used as a workaround. The race condition needs a proper fix, not a sleep-based workaround.
unmatched_gold.original_comment_excerpt: asyncio.wait is inconsistent with the task it runs first. forcing signal_to_start_request to await sleep allows listen_for_disconnect to run first (at least once).

unmatched_gold.description: `disconnect_and_get_response` can just be inlined here — it's not reused elsewhere and the extra function obscures the flow.
unmatched_gold.original_comment_excerpt: I think the `disconnect_and_get_response` code can just be inlined here.

unmatched_gold.description: Loop is unnecessary per ASGI spec: only a single http.disconnect event is allowed after body processing, so at most one event will arrive. Simplify to a single receive.
unmatched_gold.original_comment_excerpt:
I'm not sure we need the loop here. 🤔 The spec doesn't allow any `receive` events except `http.disconnect` once the body processing is completed. 

So we should get at most one event, and we can `assert message["type"] == "http.disconnect"` for that event, erroring loudly for anything else.

unmatched_gold.description: Code structure is too complex: the `zip(...)` is overkill. Use `asyncio.create_task(...)` instead of `ensure_future(...)`, and write the tasks list directly without the zip.
unmatched_gold.original_comment_excerpt:
This structure is too complex. The `zip` is overkill. 
Why `ensure_future` rather than `create_task`? 

```
tasks = [
    asyncio.create_task(self.listen_for_disconnect(receive)),
    asyncio.create_task(self.run_get_response(request)),
]
```

unmatched_gold.description: Pending task may need to be cancelled. There should be a test that exercises a view cleaning up after itself on disconnect; this is also user-facing documentation material.

There should be a test for a view cleaning up after itself. (This will feed into docs for this... — _"If you have a long running request, you may need to clean up in case the client disconnects before you're finished..."_)

unmatched_gold.description: Refactor the test: put the slow `time.sleep(...)` inside a view function in urls.py, not inline in the test, so the test can send the disconnect before the view finishes (matching the real disconnect-during-long-view scenario).
unmatched_gold.original_comment_excerpt: Create a view function that has this delay in it, rather than in the test, so that we can send the disconnect before the view finishes. See the `urls.py` sibling to this file.

unmatched_gold.description: Design choice: prefer letting the assertion-style programming error propagate uncaught (re-raised) rather than catching it as RequestAborted, since this would only happen on a buggy protocol server.
unmatched_gold.original_comment_excerpt:
We **could** handle this with `RequestAborted` above but it would be a programming error in the protocol server (e.g. Daphne/Uvicorn) and I'd just want to be uncaught/re-raised. (It's a genuine _should **never** happen_, so an assertion is the right option.) 

(We could drop it entirely... equally
